title: DUMBO District Digital Twin
summary: A walkable, browser-renderable digital twin of the DUMBO neighbourhood in Brooklyn, built from authoritative NYC open data with every asset traceable to a registered source.

narrative.problem: Two teams were building two 3D viewers, of the DUMBO district and of the Manhattan Bridge, and the central risk was duplicated geometry and incompatible coordinates. A district model also needs every building, tree and surface traceable to a source someone can check.
narrative.decision: The district contains no bridge geometry: it interoperates with the Manhattan Bridge twin through shared contracts, a common viewer kernel and coordinate frame, and a module manifest that is the entire dependency surface between the projects.
narrative.tradeoff: The Manhattan Bridge does not appear on the published site, because its assets belong to the other module; the viewer shows an integration notice and a labelled placeholder instead.
narrative.limitation: Bridge placement is provisional. Photograph classification needs a person, because the automatic screen cannot reliably tell an office interior from a street view, and tree canopy form and seasonal colour are plausible for the genus rather than measured.
narrative.caveat: The Manhattan Bridge is not shown on the published site; the viewer renders the district alone and displays an integration notice.
